chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not strike your faces with water with a striking motion when you perform your Ablution (Wudu), but gently splash the water with a gentle splashing.'
ai.seo_question: How should one wash the face during Wudu according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the physical manner of washing the face during Wudu, contrasting the forceful 'striking' (darb) with the gentle 'splashing' (shann), a distinction often discussed in Shia fiqh regarding the completeness of the wash. It reflects the Prophetic tradition of moderation (wasatiyyah) in ritual acts, ensuring that the act of purification remains dignified and thorough without being excessive or harsh.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from his father, from Ibn Al Mugheira, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Do not wipe your faces with the water with striking when you perform your Ablution (Wudhu)s, but gently splash the water with a gentle splashing’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from his father from ibn al-Mughirah from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “Do not strike water against your face when taking Wudu’. Allow the water to flow over your face.’”
